knowledge_point.title: Identifying a Possible Slope Field Based on the Type of Equation

question.:question/problem: Which of the following could be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x y?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the slope varies with both $x$ and $y.$

Of the given slope fields, the only one that varies with both $x$ and $y$ is the following:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186172040/workspace/evidence/assets/17592186172040/plots/4e472f0fcb64d0d53ce1401ad6ee3e134a54837d96da5b899c97c18146c1341e.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a vertical line and a horizontal line, the slopes vary if we move along either of the two lines.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186172040/workspace/evidence/assets/17592186172040/plots/045525575c74f776ec759ff440a4c7e1fb994cbf9305e7b2cebb74bce9030cb8.png)
